Extortion City

By: Catherine Rice | Commission

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Extortion is a problem throughout South Africa, but Cape Town has become it's epicentre, with violent criminal syndicates operating across the city.

Unique Selling Point:
A Cape Town business owner speaks out about his experiences with gangs demanding protection fees. After refusing to pay for two years, his bouncer was murdered in 2015. It was a clear message. Randolf Jorberg is now leaving South Africa, after an exclusive interview with Carte Blanche about what has been happening in this shadow economy for decades.

Summary:
Extortion rackets and gang violence are not new in Cape Town. Alleged crime bosses Mark Lifman, and Nafiz Modack are currently on trial in two separate cases. They are allegedly the kingpins of criminal syndicates operating in the city. Ralph Stanfield, leader of the "The Firm" is also currently facing a range of charges including extortion and murder. We speak to Randolf Jorberg, the owner of a bar in Long Street, who refused to pay protection fees until his bouncer was murdered in 2015.

Further information:
Jorberg started paying protection fees three days after his bouncer was murdered in 2015. He has evidence of intimidation on CCTV footage as well as audio recordings, yet he has never been called as a witness in any of the cases against alleged underworld kingpins. He was also on a hitlist that included anti-gang unit detective Charl Kinnear who was shot dead several years ago.

Script:


VO 1 A night that began like any other on one of Cape Town’s most recognised streets ended in the cold blooded murder of a doorman at a popular bar

VO 2 This is the story of what may have led to that apparently senseless killing in June 2015…not fully told until now. It reveals the inner workings of a criminal enterprise that still holds the city’s business owners to ransom.

CUT TO BLACK

VO 3 Long street is famous for it’s nightlife…a magnet for partygoers..

VO 4 It’s a place where petty criminals lurk in the shadows constantly on the look out for opportunities…….but also a place ultimately controlled by underworld crime bosses.

VO 5 Randolf Jorberg opened the Beer House bar here in 2013.

UPSOUND Randolf Jorberg (clip 30824 / 4 July / Night) Time code: 05:05 On the first night we had a queue around the block Time code: 05:14 we were a hit from the first day on. But, also on the second or third day of trade, a little shadow entered the light.

VO 6 Approached by a stranger, he was offered so called protection – paying protection fees means giving money to criminals in exchange for their promise of safety and security…..
Randolf turned down the offer.

VO 7 Now, he’s speaking out about what happened in the weeks before the murder of his doorman – but asked us not to broadcast it until he’d safely left the country.

NATSOUND I like your beard man, Thanks man.

UPSOUND Randolf Jorberg Clip 30824 Time code 05:29 The so called underworld arrived at Beer House . I was greeted by a guy with very wide shoulders, very firm handshake, and I was made to listen to a pitch for a product that I saw zero value in.
(Clip 30824 / 4 July) Time code 08:02 I’ve got a strong sense of justice, and if you are trying to sell me bullshit, I won’t buy it.

VO 8 It was common knowledge among Long Street business owners, that everyone paid protection fees. But, for two years, the Beer House steadfastly refused… until 2015.

UPSOUND Randolf Jorberg / Clip 30824 Time code : 10:37 Nine guys walked into Beer House, Time 10:51 They intentionally intimidated a guest. Time code 11:02 They fairly quickly without us asking started leaving and when leaving they pushed our doorman Time code: 11:34 That was the first time there was a very clear intention visible. (CCTV FOOTAGE emailed to you)

VO 9 Joe Kanyona, BeerHouse’s doorman had been the victim of that assault.

GOVAN: Tell me about Joe.

UPSOUND Randolf Clip 30824 25:46 Joe wasn’t the loudest. He wasn’t the quietest. He was a very friendly soul. Time code 26:01 He wasn’t the tallest, but he was friendly and welcoming. And he represented BeerHouse and was the face of the brand.

VO 10 This incident gave Randolf a taste of what was to come. Shortly afterwards, the protection offer was repeated and this time the conversation was recorded.

AUDIO RECORDING (CCTV footage of them talking as well) (Will need subtitles)
Hussain Time code 02:21 As you know I run Long Street, Loop street, most of the clubs in town.
Hussain 08:16 I’m not here to do extortion or to threaten you, you want to be with me and need my service, you’re welcome.
Hussain: 24:19 If I want to play dirty I can play dirty with you.
Hussain Time code 24:41 I’ve been in this game for 21 years
Randolph: Time code 26:09 Again, the only danger I ever saw that you promised to protect myself from is that you actually walked in is the danger that you walked in with, these people from Joburg after you told them that we are a non paying customer this is not a deal I’m willing to take.
Randolf: 27:40 But then what do I pay for?
Hussain 27:47 Backup fees, Service fees, management fees, I don’t know what you want to call it.

VO 11 The man in the recording is Hussain Taleb, a martial arts expert, who had been involved in nightclub security for decades. Known as Hussain the Morrocan, he’d been WITH the men who’d assaulted Joe just days before.

UPSOUND Randolf Clip 30824 (04/07/2024) 12:19 Now I had it as a fact it was extortion. It wasn’t just hearsay on the streets. It was real.
GOVAN: What did you do?
UPSOUND 12:30 I asked my manager to go to the Hawks and open a case.

VO 12 Doorman Joe Kanyona was to be a witness in the case of intimidation. (photos of Joe)

VO 13 But, on the night of the 20th of June, 2015, he was surrounded by four men and fatally stabbed in the neck.

LINK Three of the alleged hitmen were arrested. In court, it emerged they were paid a thousand rand to commit the crime, but the fourth man, the killer…was never identified. Neither was the alleged mastermind.

VO 14 For Randolf, the message was now clear.

UPSOUND Randolf Time Clip 30824 code 19:57 Within the first twenty four hours, my management told me they would walk out if I was now not agreeing to pay the racketeers. 20:46 Quickly afterwards, they approached us, we were like yes we now pay. Time code 21:00 They hide it as a legitimate business, they give you an invoice, they are a fully registered security company.

VO 15 The Beer House was now protected.

VO 16 But, in 2017, violence erupted on Long Street and in other areas in a battle over nightclub security. Gang shootings spilled into the streets as newcomer to the scene and alleged underworld boss Nafiz Modack moved in to take control.

UPSOUND Caryn Dolley / Journalist Time code 18:43 There was an alleged takeover, we can confidently say something happened given the number of shootings there were. But, if allegations put forward by the state are to be believed, two main groups were vying for control.

VO 17 Those two groups – The Modack Enterprise and the Lifman Group, headed by another alleged underworld kingpin, Mark Lifman – already infamous on Long Street.

V0 18 Investigative journalist and author Caryn Dolley was covering the chaos.

VO 19 Her coverage of the protection rackets would make her a target. In August 2017, she received her first death threat.

UPSOUND Caryn Dolley Clip 31128 Time code: 21:17 At the time when I received the message, I was panicked. I also didn’t quite understand what was happening
UPSOUND Caryn Dolley Time code: 19:38 I remember that was an exceptionally busy time for me as a journalist, and it was also mindblowing that these incidents kept happening.
GOVAN: Did you ever have to hire personal security? 20:14 A former employer did provide me with private security twice.
17:01 Do you think journalists are off limits?
UPSOUND: realistically and in reality anyone can become a target in an instant.

VO 20 She continued to cover the violence playing out between alleged underworld kingpins Modack and Lifman. Not just limited to the city centre, shootings erupted across Cape Town.

LINK (clip 31117 / Khayelitsha Day 2) Even here on the world famous strip in Camps Bay at Cafe Caprice an alleged hit was attempted. Two people were injured at the height of the turf war in 2017.. Those details are only just emerging in the trial of alleged underworld boss Mark Lifman…he’s currently out on bail.

VO 21 Randolf was also receiving death threats as the battle for control of the city raged on…Two factions were now demanding protection fees from Randolf.

Govan Clip 30825 / 06:10 What did the death threats say?
Randolf 06:13 They referred to my house, they referred to my daughter. They were sent to my team warning them not to work for me.

VO 22 The Covid lockdowns in 2020 gave Randolf and other business owners a reprieve from the protection rackets, but when the regulations relaxed, the crime syndicates too were back in business.

VO 23 Many business owners were able to negotiate a discount, but nobody was given an option not to pay. Randolf also resumed payments.

VO24 A hit list discovered during a police investigation, featured the name of anti gang unit detective Charl Kinnear. He was assassinated outside his house in 2020 – a murder for which Nafiz Modack is now standing trial among a litany of other alleged crimes including extortion. His arrest in 2021 followed that of his long time alleged nemesis, Mark Lifman, who also faces numerous charges including murder and conspiracy to commit murder. Both have pleaded not guilty..

VO 25 Randolf remained out of the country for several years during and after Covid…until recently. He’s decided to sell his shares in the Beer House. He feels there will not be justice until the mastermind behind Joe’s death is behind bars.

VO 26 He’s still in contact with Joe’s daughter, who was just four months old at the time of her father’s death.

UPSOUND Randolf: Clip 30824 Time code: 24:29 It will be my job one day to explain to her, and look into her eyes and say it is my fault or my decision that led to the death of her dad.

VO 27 Randolf continues to carry guilty for what happened.

UPSOUND: Randolf Clip 30826 Time code 03:42 I always handed over every CCTV material to any cop who asked. I did that plenty of times. And well…You are first people I’m sharing this with in past couple of years and talking to about it

VO 28 Does this mean light will never be shed on Joe’s murder in 2015? Will it simply be forgotten?

PAUSE

VO 29 And what impact have the arrests of these alleged crime bosses had on Cape Town’s nightlife?

Govan: Clip 30826 Time code 08:40 Now that the kingpins are on trial has anything changed on the street?
UPSOUND Randolf Clip 30826 Time code 08:46 No nothing changes, the money collectors come regularly making their rounds.

VO 30 Both Modack and Lifman declined to comment on the allegations through their lawyers.

VO 31 As for Hussain Taleb, he initially agreed to do an on camera interview.
Time code: 17:16 AUDIO “I did nothing to nobody, you can come to my house, you can come, no problem”. But cancelled at the last minute.

VO 32 He denied ever having worked for Modack or Lifman, and said he has no knowledge of who was behind Joe’s murder.

VO 33 We asked police to respond to the allegations that protection payments are continuing as usual, despite all their breakthroughs. In a written response, they said the possibility that extortionists are controlled from inside prison can’t be excluded, but they’re confident they can root out the problem completely.

ON SCREEN: “..the possibility that extortionists are controlled from inside prison cannot be excluded. As our investigation unfolds, more arrests can be affected and we will get to the bottom of the phenomena to root it out completely”,

GOVAN Time code: 14:00 (clip 30825) Why have you specified that we should only broadcast this once you’ve left the country?
UPSOUND Randolf Clip 30824 (Randolf intvw) Time code 14:08 I know what these guys are capable of.

VO 34 With Randolf safely out of the country and his full story now made public, our investigation takes us beyond Long Street and the glitz of Cape Town’s night life.

LINK So now we know extortion is rife in Cape Town. But, it’s not just happening in the city. In an upcoming episode, we examine this growing crime trend in Khayelitsha.

UPSOUND The shooting was happening here in the barber shot.. broad daylight
UPSOUND If you don’t pay they come and shoot you, that’s how much they don’t care.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Extortion is a problem throughout South Africa, but Cape Town has become it's epicentre, with violent criminal syndicates operating across the city.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: A Cape Town business owner speaks out about his experiences with gangs demanding protection fees. After refusing to pay for two years, his bouncer was murdered in 2015. It was a clear message. Randolf Jorberg is now leaving South Africa, after an exclusive interview with Carte Blanche about what has been happening in this shadow economy for decades.
metadata.Summary: Extortion rackets and gang violence are not new in Cape Town. Alleged crime bosses Mark Lifman, and Nafiz Modack are currently on trial in two separate cases. They are allegedly the kingpins of criminal syndicates operating in the city. Ralph Stanfield, leader of the "The Firm" is also currently facing a range of charges including extortion and murder. We speak to Randolf Jorberg, the owner of a bar in Long Street, who refused to pay protection fees until his bouncer was murdered in 2015.
metadata.Further information: Jorberg started paying protection fees three days after his bouncer was murdered in 2015. He has evidence of intimidation on CCTV footage as well as audio recordings, yet he has never been called as a witness in any of the cases against alleged underworld kingpins. He was also on a hitlist that included anti-gang unit detective Charl Kinnear who was shot dead several years ago.
